title: Non-overlapping Intervals
prompt:
The library has one reading room and a list of requested bookings [start, end]. You want to honour as many as possible. Return the minimum number of bookings to remove so the rest do not overlap.

Bookings that only touch ([1, 2] and [2, 3]) do not overlap.

Write eraseOverlapIntervals(intervals).

  • eraseOverlapIntervals([[1, 2], [2, 3], [3, 4], [1, 3]]) returns 1 (remove [1, 3])
  • eraseOverlapIntervals([[1, 2], [1, 2], [1, 2]]) returns 2
  • eraseOverlapIntervals([[1, 2], [2, 3]]) returns 0

Constraints: 0 to 105 intervals; start < end; values can be negative. Target: O(n log n).

tests.name: one long booking blocks many short ones: remove the long one
tests.code: assertEqual(eraseOverlapIntervals([[1, 100], [1, 2], [3, 4], [5, 6], [7, 8]]), 1, 'sorting by START would keep [1,100] and remove 4; sort by END');

tests.name: negatives and a chain of overlaps

hints: Trigger: "maximum number of non-overlapping intervals" or "minimum to remove" = the classic sort by end time greedy (activity selection).

Keeping as many as possible is the same as removing as few as possible. Sort by end. Walk through: if a booking starts at or after the end of the last one you kept, keep it. Otherwise skip it (count it as removed).

Shape:

sorted.sort((a, b) => a[1] - b[1]);
let kept = 0, lastEnd = -Infinity;
for (const [start, end] of sorted) {
  if (start >= lastEnd) { kept++; lastEnd = end; }
}
return intervals.length - kept;
explain:
Time O(n log n) for the sort, O(n) for the pass. Space O(n) for the sorted copy (O(1) extra if you sort in place). Why end time? The booking that finishes first uses up the least of the future, so choosing it can never make things worse. That "can never make it worse" argument is what makes a greedy choice safe.

Say it: "This is activity selection. I'll sort by end time and greedily keep each booking that starts after the last kept one ends. Removals = total minus kept. O(n log n)."
